comment: Every difference between doors that the door contracts allow. An entry names the facts it excuses (harness/doors/compare.ts), says why in words a person building an app can act on, and names who decides whether it stays. `deliberate` is meant; `drift` is not meant and not yet fixed. An entry that excuses nothing fails the comparison, so this list can't outlive the differences.

differences.why: A box exports with its own command (`parachute-vault export`); cloud-style doors stream the same files from `GET /api/export`. The files themselves are compared and equal (exit/file.*). An app that offers "download my vault" can do it over HTTP on cloud only.

Asking the account door for a vault that isn't yours: cloud answers 403 `not_owner` whether or not the name exists, so one account can't probe another's vault names. A box has one account and answers 404 `vault_not_found`. Treat both as "not yours".

A vault credential minted through the account door lasts 90 days on a box and 15 minutes on cloud. An app must read `expires_at` and mint again; one that stores the credential works for months on a box and breaks in a quarter of an hour on cloud.

The account door's replies share `name`, `url`, `vault_token` and `services["vault:<name>"]` on every door, and the contracts hold those. Beyond them each door adds its own: cloud lists `vault_id`, `created_at`, `mcp_url`, `usage` and a second `services.vault` key; a box lists `caps`, `version` and `token_guidance`; the delete reply reports each runtime's own clean-up. Build on the shared fields; derive the MCP address as `<url>/mcp`.

differences.owner: Aaron (also audit L2-10: should an AI connector be offered admin at all)
differences.why: Both doors grant `vault:<name>:admin` to an app that asks and is approved. A box lists it in `scopes_supported`; cloud lists only read and write. A connector that asks for what is advertised can declare types on a box and not on cloud.

differences.owner: 0.9.0 cloud parity (audit L1-01, delta 36): the AI-facing text moves into the engine
differences.why: A model connecting to a box is told the vault's address, how to query, how files move and how to script it (seven sections). On cloud it gets the description and one line. A refused tool call's message starts with `[error_type]` on a box only; the code and the structured `data` are the same on both.

differences.owner: spec §8 (keys): on cloud a key is an approved OAuth app, managed in the account
differences.why: A box's admin sees `manage-token` (and from 0.9 `manage-keys`) for the hub's own key store. Cloud-style doors have no hub key store: connections and named keys are listed and revoked through the account door.

The 401 from MCP names the protected-resource document at `/vault/<name>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` on a box and at `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/vault/<name>/mcp` on cloud. Both addresses answer with the same document on every door (held by mcp/protected-resource.at.*), so a client that follows the header works everywhere.

differences.owner: audit L1-08: one seed in the engine
differences.why: A new vault holds the same starter notes on every door. A box also declares a `capture` type; cloud doesn't.
Cloud's vault info carries what the plan allows: `cap_bytes`, `caps`, and voice minutes left. A box has no plans.

differences.owner: 0.9.3 one settings file and admin API
differences.why: `GET /vault/<name>` shows `embeddings` and `transcription` on cloud only; `GET /api/vault` shows `embeddings.state` on a box only. An app that shows whether semantic search is ready reads a different field per door.

differences.owner: T-430 (the personal door): a browser sign-in for an owner who holds only a key
differences.why: On a personal door the owner signs in with a Nostr key at `POST /account/token` and nowhere else, so there is no browser session to approve an app on the consent screen. A consumer AI app that connects by OAuth (Claude's connectors, any app that follows the MCP sign-in) can't be approved there; apps use a named key from `/account/keys` instead. Discovery and registration answer as on a box.
differences.note: Covers every fact the approval contracts record, because none of them can run on a personal door today. When the personal door gains a browser sign-in, delete this entry rather than narrowing it: each of those facts must then be equal or named on its own.

differences.owner: core 0.9.1 keys (T-414): one way to link and list a sign-in key
differences.why: A cloud-style door lists and links the account's sign-in keys at `/account/pubkeys` with the account credential. A box does it in its browser session at `/api/account/pubkeys` (a challenge, then the password again for the first key). Signing in with a linked key is the same call on both.

differences.owner: this change, once the 0.9 branch takes `next`
differences.why: The box's missing MCP headers in CORS are fixed on `next` beside these contracts. The 0.9 branch was cut before that and gets it when it takes `next`.

A revoked app key gets 401 at once on both doors. The body differs: a box's hub answers `{error: "invalid_token", error_description}`, a cloud-style door's vault answers `{error: "Unauthorized", message}`; and the revoke reply carries `refused_now` on a cloud-style door only. Branch on the 401.

differences.owner: parachute-cloud, at its next core pin: call refuseTypesInTags (core tag-kind.ts) in rest/records.ts and pass it to addRecordTools in mcp-09.ts, or move rest/records.ts onto core's rest-records.ts
differences.why: On the record door `tags` holds plain labels (SPEC §2.4). From 0.9.1 a box refuses a type's name in `tags` with 422 `tag_kind` and the fix (`types: [...]`), on `/api/records` and on create-record/update-record, and writes nothing. The personal door still accepts it and files the name as the type. Send a type's name in `types`: that works on both.

differences.owner: parachute-cloud 0.9.1 follow-up: the cloud vault worker's twin of the write stamp (call core write-stamp.ts resolveBy, read the top-level `key` claim (the personal door mints `permissions.app_key`) and enforce `permissions.acts_for`) and identity's mint of on_behalf_of
differences.why: A key the owner lets write on behalf of others (`POST /account/keys {..., on_behalf_of: true}`) stamps `by <key name>:<id>` from the `Parachute-On-Behalf-Of` header or the MCP `on_behalf_of` parameter, and a key without the grant is refused. The box has it; the personal door's mint refuses the field and its vault worker would accept a token carrying `acts_for` without enforcing it, so the contracts don't run there.
differences.note: When the cloud vault worker has the twin, delete this entry rather than narrowing it.

differences.owner: parachute-cloud, at its next core pin: record the key's kind (core write-stamp.ts rememberKeyKind) when it reads the key's name; identity mints `permissions.app_key` with no kind yet
differences.why: Each kept revision says what kind of key replaced it (`via_kind`: person, agent, app, service) on the box. The personal door's revisions carry `via key:<name>` but no kind yet.
